$comment: Hand-written English meanings for the Query, Flow, Event and Function nouns of docs/DSL_KEYWORD_REFERENCE.md. See meanings-concept.json for the file format.

query.summary: A named, parameterised read over one concept. It filters, orders and limits rows, may join through reference fields, and may group and aggregate. A query never widens access: row-level access of the concept still applies.

queryLookup.summary: A per-key aggregate over another concept, merged into each grouped row of the query as an extra output column.

queryComputedColumn.summary: An output column computed per grouped row from other output columns.

groupByField.summary: One `groupBy` entry of a query: a plain field name, or an object `{field, bucket}` that buckets a date or datetime field to day, week, month, quarter or year. The field may also be a join through a chain of reference fields (for example `customer.region`).

aggregateFunction.summary: One aggregate output column of a grouped query.

queryParameter.summary: A named, typed parameter. Used as a `query.parameters` entry (and, for the legacy procedures, as a `procedure.parameters` entry).

flow.summary: Something the app does: an ordered list of steps started by a trigger. A flow is durable (each step is checkpointed, and a flow can wait for an event or a human), can compensate with `onFailure`, and is the only place where behavior is written. Exactly one of `steps` or (for a specializing flow) `hooks` must be present; `input` needs `steps` or `specializes`.

flowInput.summary: Declares that the flow's input has the shape of a concept's request body, for a given mode.

flowSchedule.summary: Recurring start of a flow: a cron expression and the tenants it runs for. The scheduler starts the flow like an HTTP call, under the system principal.

flowHook.summary: Extra steps inserted before or after a named step of the flow being specialized. Lets an app extend a flow it got from a pack without copying it.

flowStep.summary: One step of a flow. `type` decides what the step does and which other keywords it uses; the schema requires the keywords listed under Conditional rules for each type. Steps reference earlier results with `$name.field` flow-state references and use the one expression language for conditions.

awaitMatch.summary: How an arriving event is matched to a parked `awaitEvent` step.

humanTask.summary: Turns an `awaitEvent` step into a task in a person's inbox. The flow resumes when the person picks an outcome and fills the form.

event.summary: A named fact that happened. Declared at the model root or inside a concept; flows publish it with `emitEvent` or `scheduleEvent`, are triggered by it (`trigger.event`) or wait for it (`awaitEvent`). A concept-nested event with `mode` is also published automatically by the generated create, update or delete.

eventPayloadField.summary: One field of an event's payload.

function.summary: A named pure function callable from any expression, for example `surgeMultiplier(open, free)`. The call is replaced by the body at compile time. A function may not read a row field and may not call itself. A pack's functions are called `pack::name`.

slots.query.name: The query's name, unique within the model; screens, panels, flows and agents refer to it by this name.
slots.query.concept: The concept whose rows the query reads.
slots.query.where: Filter expression over the concept's fields and the query parameters (`$user.id` is available). Row-level access of the concept always applies on top.
slots.query.orderBy: Fields to sort by, first sorts first. Each entry is a field or output column name, optionally followed by a direction.
slots.query.parameters: The query's declared parameters; callers bind them by name.
slots.query.permissionRequirements: Permissions a caller must hold to run the query.
slots.query.metadata: Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged.
slots.query.groupBy: Fields (or date buckets, or reference paths) that group the rows. Makes the query an aggregate query.
slots.query.aggregates: Aggregate output columns (count, sum, avg, min, max) computed per group.
slots.query.having: Filter over the grouped output columns, applied after grouping, lookups and computed columns.
slots.queryComputedColumn.name: Name of the computed output column.
slots.aggregateFunction.name: Name of the output column.
slots.aggregateFunction.field: The field the function reads (not used by `count`).
slots.queryParameter.name: The parameter's name; callers bind it by this name and the query refers to it as `$name`.
slots.queryParameter.type: The parameter's type, a field type name such as `string`, `int`, `date` or `uuid`.
slots.queryParameter.required: True: the caller must supply it (unless a `defaultExpression` exists).
slots.flow.name: The flow's name, unique within the model. It addresses the flow in the API (`/api/flows/<name>/execute`), in `callFlow` steps, screen buttons and agent exposures.
slots.flow.concept: The concept the flow works on by default; concept steps without their own `scope` use it.
slots.flow.specializes: Name of a base flow (typically from a pack) that this flow specializes; it may then add `hooks` instead of declaring all `steps`.
slots.flow.input: Declares that the flow's input is shaped like a concept body (see `flowInput`).
slots.flow.outputSchema: A `schemaObject` describing the flow's output (the value of its `return` step).
slots.flow.action: How a button that starts this flow is presented (label, confirmation, danger level).
slots.flow.startEndpoint: Whether the generated app offers a start endpoint for the flow. `expose` is the current way to control who may start it.
slots.flow.metadata: Binds an author-supplied, hash-pinned Java class to the flow instead of its steps. Holds `untrustedExtensionEntrypoint`.
slots.flow.hooks: Steps to run before or after named steps of the specialized base flow.
slots.flow.steps: The ordered steps, at least one. Required unless the flow specializes another and only adds hooks.
slots.flowHook.targetStep: Name of the step of the base flow the hook attaches to.
slots.flowHook.steps: The steps to insert, at least one.
slots.flowStep.name: The step's name: unique within the flow, shown in traces, and the way a hook's `targetStep` refers to the step.
slots.flowStep.type: What the step does. `invariantCheck` evaluates invariants; `capabilityCall` calls a capability operation; `generatedAction` runs a generated action; `createConcept`, `updateConcept`, `deleteConcept`, `readConcept`, `listConcepts` and `runQuery` work with concepts and queries; `emitEvent` publishes an event now and `scheduleEvent` later; `awaitEvent` parks until an event arrives; `branch` chooses between step lists; `forEach` loops; `map` and `set` compute values; `callFlow` starts another flow; `notify` sends a notification; `return` ends the flow with a value.
slots.flowStep.checkpoint: On an `invariantCheck`: `pre` or `post`, when the invariants are evaluated relative to the surrounding work.
slots.flowStep.scope: On an `invariantCheck`, `createConcept` or other concept step: the concept the step applies to.
slots.flowStep.invariants: On an `invariantCheck`: the names of the invariants to evaluate.
slots.flowStep.capability: On a `capabilityCall`: the name of the capability to call (a declared capability, or a platform one such as `notification`).
slots.flowStep.operation: On a `capabilityCall`: the operation of that capability.
slots.flowStep.input: The value handed to the step, as a flow-state reference or expression (for example `$input`). For a concept step it is the record body.
slots.flowStep.output: The flow-state key under which the step stores its result; later steps read it as `$key`.
slots.flowStep.args: On a `capabilityCall`: positional arguments, each a literal or a flow-state reference.
slots.flowStep.policy: Overrides the called operation's execution policy (retries, timeout, circuit breaker, idempotency) for this step.
slots.flowStep.event: On `emitEvent` and `scheduleEvent`: the name of the event to publish (a declared event).
slots.flowStep.from: A flow-state reference giving the step's source value: for `map` the value copied, for `emitEvent` / `scheduleEvent` the event payload (alternative to `data`).
slots.flowStep.data: An object built in place - a map from name to literal or flow-state reference - used as the event payload of `emitEvent` / `scheduleEvent` instead of `from`.
slots.flowStep.condition: On a `branch`: the expression that chooses `then` (true) or `else` (false).
slots.flowStep.action: How the step is presented in traces and action histories (label, danger level).
slots.flowStep.actionName: On a `generatedAction`: the name of the generated action to run.
slots.flowStep.then: On a `branch`: the steps run when the condition is true.
slots.flowStep.else: On a `branch`: the steps run when the condition is false.
slots.flowStep.awaitEvent: On an `awaitEvent`: the name of the event the flow waits for.
slots.flowStep.awaitRef: On an `awaitEvent`: the flow-state key under which the arriving event's payload is stored.
slots.flowStep.match: On an `awaitEvent`: how an arriving event is matched to this flow instance.
slots.flowStep.delaySeconds: On a `scheduleEvent`: seconds to wait before the event is published.
slots.flowStep.value: On a `return`: the value the flow ends with. On a `set`: the expression whose result is stored in `output`.
slots.flowInput.concept: The concept whose request body the flow's input mirrors.
slots.flowSchedule.cron: The cron expression: classic 5 fields (minute hour day month weekday) or Spring's 6 fields with seconds.
slots.flowSchedule.tenantScope: A tenant id or a list of tenant ids the flow runs for, one independent schedule per tenant. Omitted means the default tenant.
slots.awaitMatch.correlation: True: only an event carrying the same correlation id as this flow instance resumes it.
slots.awaitMatch.payload: A map from event payload field to an expression; the event matches only when each field equals the value of its expression.
slots.humanTask.description: Longer text shown with the task in the inbox.
slots.humanTask.assignee: Who may complete the task: a specific user (a flow-state reference) and/or one or more roles.
slots.humanTask.outcomes: The buttons the person can choose from, at least one; the chosen value is stored under `outcomeField`.
slots.humanTask.fields: The form fields the person fills in; their values are delivered with the completed event.
slots.event.name: The event's name, unique within the model; the string flows publish, trigger on and await.
slots.event.specializes: Name of a base event (typically from a pack) this event specializes.
slots.event.version: Version label of the event's payload contract.
slots.event.payload: The payload fields: each a field name string or an object with a name and a type.
slots.eventPayloadField.name: The payload field's name.
slots.eventPayloadField.type: The payload field's type (a scalar field type).
slots.function.description: A sentence describing what the function computes.

inline.function.params.name: The parameter's name, used in the body.
inline.function.params.type: The parameter's type (the same names as `returns`).
inline.flow.trigger.event: Name of the event whose publication starts the flow.
inline.flow.trigger.condition: Optional expression over `$event` that must be true for the event to start the flow.
inline.flow.trigger.schedule: A `flowSchedule` (cron and tenant scope): the flow starts on that schedule.
inline.flow.trigger.webhook: Name of a capability that declares an `inbound` door; the flow starts on every verified delivery to that door.
inline.humanTask.assignee.roles: Role names; any user holding one of them may complete the task.
inline.humanTask.outcomes.value: The outcome value stored when this button is chosen.
inline.humanTask.outcomes.label: The caption of the button.
inline.humanTask.fields.name: The form field's name; its value arrives under this key.
inline.humanTask.fields.label: The caption of the form field.
inline.humanTask.fields.required: True: the person must fill the field in.
inline.humanTask.fields.maxLength: Maximum length of a text value.
inline.groupByField.field: The date or datetime field (or reference path) to group by.
inline.groupByField.bucket: The time bucket the values are truncated to: day, week, month, quarter or year.
